selected_problem: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. Fresh-main inspection found that basename-only test/source matching created a `tests` edge from one test to every non-test file with the same logical stem. A repository containing `src/index.js`, `lib/index.js`, and `tests/index.test.js` therefore fabricated two ownership edges without evidence for either relationship, distorting semantic centrality and context selection.

execution.route_basis: The fresh canonical main exposes one narrow falsifiable semantic-graph integrity defect. Source-contract replay therefore narrows it to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without prescribing a new test-discovery architecture or forcing mode rotation.

changes: A test/source stem relationship now emits a `tests` edge only when exactly one non-test source candidate matches the logical stem.
Ambiguous same-stem ownership fails closed instead of fabricating multiple semantic edges.
The previous unique colocated `.test` / `.spec` linkage and deterministic relative-import behavior remain covered by regressions.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED against fresh main: `tests/index.test.js` produced two `tests` edges, one to `src/index.js` and one to `lib/index.js`, solely from basename equality.

truth_boundaries: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. This fails closed on ambiguous basename-only test ownership; it does not infer framework-specific test ownership when several sources are plausible.
Tests that intentionally cover several same-stem modules will not receive heuristic `tests` edges without stronger evidence; avoiding false semantic claims is preferred to fabricating ownership.
Semantic-context neighborhood selection remains bounded and does not prove globally optimal context selection for arbitrary software goals.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
